newsitem.title: USA: Commerce nominee Daley defends department.
newsitem.headline: Commerce nominee Daley defends department.

text.p: Commerce Secretary nominee William Daley promised on Wednesday to keep politics out of his department and said it was essential to maintaining a strong U.S. economy.
Daley also said he would support sanctions against China if Beijing engaged in weapons proliferation activities.

"I want to make my position absolutely clear; there is no place for politics in the Department of Commerce," Daley, 48, said in written answers to questions submitted to him before his confirmation hearing at the Senate Commerce Committee. The questions and answers were released by the committee.
Daley was nominated by President Bill Clinton last month to succeed Mickey Kantor, who replaced Ron Brown after Brown was killed in a plane crash last April on a trip to Bosnia.

Some former Commerce Department officials are being investigated for political campaign fundraising activity while at or after they left the department and critics have said too many department posts have been used for political appointees.
"The department's reputation has been sullied," Commerce Committee Chairman John McCain, an Arizona Republican, told Daley.

"If confirmed, there will be no connection between campaign contributions and making decisions on important departmental programmes, including participation in trade missions," Daley said in his written answers.

He said he would suspend all trade missions for 30 days while the procedures for deciding which business executives go on the trips were being reviewed. He also said he would cut the 196 political positions at the department by 100.

Asked about the use of laws calling for trade sanctions against China if China engages in military proliferation activities, Daley replied, "I support implementing those laws and imposing sanctions if the facts of Chinese behaviour meet the test in the laws."
Daley said he would insist on open and fair trade. "We shouldn't leave our workers at risk from unfair trading partners. I can't be aggressive enough," he said

Daley defended the department against congressional critics who say it serves little purpose and should be abolished. He said it was essential for promoting trade and providing reliable economic information.
"The Commerce Department is where America's potential and promise come together, where our future jobs are created and our economic growth is nurtured," Daley said.
Committee members praised Daley and McCain said he expected Daley to be confirmed by the Senate in a week or two.
"You're smart, you're tough, you know how to get things done," said Louisiana Democrat John Bureaux.

Daley, a Chicago lawyer, is the brother of Chicago Mayor Richard Daley. He helped Clinton win passage of the North American Free Trade Agreement and helped organise last year's Democratic Party Convention in Chicago.
